solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cat trapping right clavicle, say, in instrument (8)

indicatorNotes.trapping: the cat holds the R inside itself, as a trap holds its catch

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
R = right; it goes inside TOM after the T
the clavicle is one example of a bone

annotation.surface: A cat has somehow got a collarbone stuck inside a musical instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the clavicle as an example, so you want the category it belongs to, not the word itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the trombone is one member of the brass section, so 'instrument' names its class.

entries.clue: Gallery of rubbish — English? (4)

blocks.note: tat = cheap rubbish
E = English

annotation.surface: Someone sneers that a gallery is full of junk, wondering whether it is the English kind.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tate is the family of national galleries in Britain, the best known being Tate Britain and Tate Modern in London.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Tate is one particular gallery, Britain's national collection of modern and British art.

entries.clue: Weight to ruin a chef, regularly ignored (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly ignored: every other letter is skipped at a steady rhythm, leaving the rest

blocks.note: eleven letters; drop the 1st, 3rd, 5th and so on, keeping the even-placed ones

annotation.surface: A heavy object threatens to spoil a cook, though nobody pays attention to it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' means alternate letters; here T, R, I, A, H and F go, and O, U, N, C, E stay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the ounce is a small imperial unit, one sixteenth of a pound, so it is one kind of weight.

entries.clue: Celebrate dancing with hot unmarried woman (12)

indicatorNotes.dancing: letters that dance move about and swap places

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram fodder, 3 more letters

annotation.surface: A party scene: people celebrating on the dance floor alongside an attractive single woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot unmarried woman' reads as one phrase, but 'hot' belongs to the wordplay and the definition is only 'unmarried woman'.
annotation.definitionFit: A bachelorette is the female counterpart of a bachelor: a young woman who has not married.

entries.clue: Nato admitting one new country (6)

indicatorNotes.admitting: to admit is to let in, so NATO takes I inside

blocks.note: taken as it stands
I = one, the Roman numeral; it goes inside NATO before the O
N = new

annotation.surface: The military alliance lets in a newly formed country as a member.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost literal: Nato does admit new countries, and the answer is one of them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a nation is a people with its own state and territory, which is what 'country' means here.

entries.clue: Composer beginning to hail taxi that’s reversing (4)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the start of 'hail' is its first letter
indicatorNotes.reversing: a vehicle that is reversing goes backwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: first letter of hail
a cab is a taxi

annotation.surface: A composer tries to flag down a cab that happens to be backing up.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both pieces: H then CAB, read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Johann Sebastian Bach is one of the best-known German composers.

entries.clue: Relation of current peer (7)

blocks.note: AC = alternating current
a count is a nobleman, and a peer is a member of the nobility

annotation.surface: Someone asks how a present-day aristocrat is related to them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a family member, but here it means a telling, as in the relation of events.
annotation.definitionFit: A relation of events is an account of them: a story or report.

entries.clue: Impotent part of the LP lesson (8)

indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is a part of the letters that follow

blocks.note: the run starts after the T of 'the' and stops before the ON of 'lesson'

annotation.surface: A dismissive note that one track on the record teaching you something is feeble.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals of LP make it look like a record, which hides that its two letters simply join the word either side.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: impotent means powerless, unable to act or help oneself.

entries.clue: Express’s lead editor involved in distributing fast optical character recognition? (5,7)

indicatorNotes.lead: the lead of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.involved in: to be involved in something is to be inside it

blocks.note: to distribute something is to spread it; it opens after SP
first letter of Express
ED = editor; E and ED go together after the first two letters of SPREADING

annotation.surface: A newspaper editor is busy rolling out quick text-scanning software.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Optical character recognition' is really software that reads print; the question mark tells you to take it literally, as eyes recognising letters quickly.
annotation.definitionFit: Speed reading is quick recognition of printed characters by eye, a playful take on the name of the software.

entries.clue: What goes with gin, too nice not to finish (5)

indicatorNotes.not to finish: each word stops short of its last letter

blocks.note: TOO without its last letter
NICE without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone decides a drink is too pleasant to leave unfinished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not to finish' applies to both words, not just the last; each loses its final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: tonic water is the classic mixer poured with gin.

entries.clue: Clay pit breaking standard (7)

indicatorNotes.breaking: the letters are broken apart and put back in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Digging a clay pit has gone beyond the usual limits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Breaking standard' reads as breaking a rule, but 'standard' is the definition, an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: standard and typical both mean normal, of the usual kind.

entries.clue: Somehow he set our axle straight (12)

indicatorNotes.Somehow: the letters come together in some other way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A mechanic has somehow managed to straighten a bent axle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Straight' looks like part of the repair job; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: 'straight' is everyday slang for attracted to the opposite sex.

entries.clue: Warms up beforehand, concerned with preliminary races under pressure (8)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down answer, what is under something comes after it

blocks.note: P = pressure; it sits on top
re = concerning, as in memo headers
heats are the early races that decide who reaches the final

annotation.surface: An athlete limbers up nervously before the qualifying rounds.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'warms up' an athlete's routine; the answer is what you do to an oven.
annotation.definitionFit: To preheat an oven is to warm it up in advance, before the food goes in.

entries.clue: New version of extremely rare footwear (6)

indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its two ends

blocks.note: first and last letters of RARE
a boot is footwear

annotation.surface: A fashion house has brought out an updated version of a hard-to-find shoe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely rare' reads as 'very rare'; it means only the extreme letters of RARE.
annotation.definitionFit: A reboot is a new version of a film or series that starts it afresh.

entries.clue: Audibly jeer Kay’s smell (7)

indicatorNotes.Audibly: the answer is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: to boo is to jeer, and Kay is taken as written

annotation.surface: A heckler loudly mocks a woman named Kay for the way she smells.
annotation.walkthrough: Kay is just a name; the 's joins it to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist sense: in wine tasting the bouquet is the aroma of the wine, so it is one kind of smell.

entries.clue: Most of metal framework is free (6)

indicatorNotes.Most of: most of a word is all but its last letter

blocks.note: a grate is a metal framework; drop the last E
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: Someone is told that most of a metal structure comes at no charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is free' reads as the verb and its complement; 'is' is really letters, and 'free' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Latin: gratis means without payment, free of charge.

entries.clue: Remnant of copper wrapped in newspaper (6)

indicatorNotes.wrapped in: CU is wrapped inside the newspaper's letters

blocks.note: taken as it stands
the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; it goes inside FT

annotation.surface: A scrap of copper wire comes wrapped up in yesterday's paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like a link word joining the definition, but it supplies the first two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An offcut is a leftover piece cut from a larger material: a remnant.

entries.clue: Construction of deck that is vulnerable in high winds? (5,2,5)

annotation.definition: Construction of deck that is vulnerable in high winds?

blocks.note: the surface wants a timber deck built onto a house; the setter means something built out of a deck of playing cards

blocks.clueFragment: that is vulnerable in high winds?
blocks.note: a storm threatens the garden deck, but the setter's structure falls at the slightest draught

annotation.surface: A builder worries that a new wooden deck may not survive a storm.
annotation.walkthrough: There is no wordplay: 'deck' is a pack of cards, and the question mark flags that 'high winds' understates how little it takes to knock one down.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: cards propped against each other in tiers make a famously fragile structure.

entries.clue: US state expelling popular huntress (5)

indicatorNotes.expelling: to expel is to throw out, so IN leaves the word

blocks.note: Indiana is a US state
in = popular, fashionable; removed from the front of INDIANA

annotation.surface: An American state throws out a well-liked woman who hunts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popular' is a crossword staple for IN, as in 'the in thing'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Diana was the Roman goddess of the hunt, the huntress of myth.

entries.clue: Car manufacturer’s vehicle part (4)

blocks.note: the Spanish car maker, part of the Volkswagen group
what the driver and passengers sit on

annotation.surface: A carmaker's own component for its vehicles.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive, but it stands for 'is', linking the two meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: The word names both a Spanish brand of car and the thing you sit on inside any car.

entries.clue: A swift shortly clutching at marine? (7)

indicatorNotes.shortly: the word is cut short by its last letter
indicatorNotes.clutching: QUIC holds AT between its letters

blocks.note: taken as it stands
swift = quick, less its last letter
taken as it stands; it goes inside QUIC after the U

annotation.surface: A swift, the fast-flying bird, snatches at a soldier from the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marine' tempts as a noun, the soldier; the question mark flags it as an example of the adjective, since marine life is one kind of aquatic life.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: marine means of the sea, one sort of aquatic, living in water.

entries.clue: I, for example, am returning picture (5)

indicatorNotes.returning: to return is to come back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as it stands
e.g. = for example
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: Someone announces they are heading home as an example to others.
annotation.walkthrough: The commas make 'for example' look like an aside; it is a piece of the wordplay, and only the part after 'I' turns round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an image is a picture or likeness of something.

entries.clue: Initially, spider is tangling every part of web (4)

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these four words

annotation.surface: A spider is getting every strand of its web in a knot.
annotation.walkthrough: The spider's web is really the World Wide Web.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on 'web': the World Wide Web is made up of countless websites, each one a part of it.

entries.clue: Sluggish man who’s getting married with relative tranquillity at first (8)

indicatorNotes.at first: the first letter of the word before

blocks.note: a stag is a man about to marry, as in a stag party
nan = grandmother
first letter of tranquillity

annotation.surface: A dull groom-to-be enjoys some family calm before his wedding.
annotation.walkthrough: A stag party is the British bachelor party held just before a man's wedding.
annotation.definitionFit: Used of water, trade or an economy, stagnant means not moving or developing: sluggish.
